sections.content: How many people are "packers, bottlers, canners and fillers"?

123,000 people

were counted on the census as "packers, bottlers, canners and fillers" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Packers, bottlers, canners and fillers pack, wrap, fill, label and seal containers by hand or machine.

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "packers, bottlers, canners and fillers" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 20 to 24 years. Of the whole working population 7.9% were aged 20 to 24 years. For people working as "packers, bottlers, canners and fillers", 12.2% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "packers, bottlers, canners and fillers" was 65 years or older.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "packers, bottlers, canners and fillers" included:

  • vehicle technicians, mechanics and electricians
  • delivery operatives
  • electricians and electrical fitters

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

A similar number of men and women had this job

Among people working as "packers, bottlers, canners and fillers" there were a similar number of men and women (47.5% compared with 52.5%).

This means "packers, bottlers, canners and fillers" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "elementary trades and related occupations".

Men made up 47.5% and women made up 52.5% of "packers, bottlers, canners and fillers"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women. This occupation was one of the jobs for which the proportion of men and women was closest to this overall picture.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "packers, bottlers, canners and fillers" included:

  • social and humanities scientists
  • bakers and flour confectioners
  • dental practitioners

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "packers, bottlers, canners and fillers" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

The percentage of men and women who are "packers, bottlers, canners and fillers" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "packers, bottlers, canners and fillers", 7.4% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (75% compared with 25%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (97.7%) than self-employed (2.3%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the East Midlands. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Leicester, this is in the same region of the East Midlands.
